en: The Sūtra on the Five Terrors Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Song dynasty layman Juqu Jingsheng.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. The Buddha...
He addressed the bhikṣus:
"There are five future terrors that have not yet arrived and are not yet accomplished, yet they will arrive before long and are to be feared.
You should contemplate them well and distance yourselves from them through skillful means."
What are the five?
"First, there will be monks in the future who lack conduct and precepts in body, whose minds are unrestrained, and who lack wisdom following from their bodies;
they themselves lack conduct and precepts, their minds are unrestrained, up to lacking wisdom within."

When that person has studied up to the point of receiving the full precepts (*mahāśramaṇa-saṃvara*), they follow their teacher as a master, yet they are self-restrained, self-disciplined, and possess self-clarified wisdom.

From among those who originally followed the superior class of students, there are later students who, following the aforementioned method of initial study, subsequently violate the Vinaya and speak in slander against the Dharma-sūtras; such persons are far removed from true wisdom.
"Monks! This is the first future terror and dread that will soon arrive.
You should reflect well upon it and employ skillful means to avoid it."

"Second, there will be bhikṣus in the future who lack conduct and precepts in body, whose minds are unrestrained, and who lack wisdom; yet they shall proclaim for others that there is a hidden treasure. Teaching them in a manner that is out of sequence, lacking internal precepts, and contrary to the Honored One’s instructions, they claim that by following this one can reach the further shore, thereby leading them far from the current."
This is the second future peril that will soon arrive.
You should reflect well upon it and employ skillful means to avoid it. "Third:

there will be bhikṣus in the future who lack conduct and precepts in body, whose minds are unrestrained, and who lack wisdom; having originally had no true teacher, they receive incorrect teachings. These bhikṣus, having received such teachings, lose the meaning of the Dharma and the Vinaya."
This is the third future peril that will soon arrive.
You should contemplate it well and employ skillful means to avoid it. "The fourth is this:

in the future, there will be bhikṣus who lack conduct and precepts in body, lack restraint in mind, and lack wisdom. Because they lack conduct and precepts in body, lack restraint in mind, and lack wisdom, when they gather with other bhikṣus to recite the Vinaya and expound its meaning, they present later passages as if they were from the middle, and present middle passages as if they were from the end. Consequently, they lose their vision and enter into darkness; unable to awaken themselves, they distance themselves from the True Dharma."
This is the fourth future dread that will soon arrive.
You should reflect well upon it and employ skillful means to avoid it.

"Fifth, there will be bhikṣus who come in the future whose bodies lack practice and precepts, whose minds are unrestrained, and who lack wisdom. Because their bodies lack practice and precepts and their minds are unrestrained and devoid of wisdom, they accept all the clever words and loose speech produced by the world; seeing them recite such things, they find pleasure and delight in their minds."

Regarding what the Venerable One has taught—the twelve links of dependent origination, suffering, emptiness, and impermanence—he finds them disagreeable; he rejects them all and refuses to accept them. Hearing their teaching, his mind harbors doubts that they are not so, and he feels neither joy nor delight.
"This is the fifth future peril that will arrive before long.
You should contemplate it well and employ skillful means to avoid it.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
The Sūtra on the Five Terrifying Worlds Spoken by the Buddha
